about: Trait wordings for the mixed-document-types corpus (2026-10-09), written by Claude as corpus content; checked by doctypes.py checkwords. Four new forms besides the list profile (which keeps wordings.json of 2026-10-08-wordvar: trained headers H0-H3 and phrasings p0-p3): cv (an item under a CV section), form (a value under a form field), bio (a third-person predicate; code adds the subject 'He' or the first name), interview (a first-person clause). Groups give the section or field labels (one label variant per group per document); an item with its own 'labels' overrides its group's. No wording repeats a readout's paraphrase verb phrase (wordings.json 'para': play the cello, speak Welsh, keep bees, own a narrowboat, hold a pilot's licence, ...), carries another trait's key word, uses a negation morpheme, or shares a non-key word or bigram with any held-out p4 phrasing. Since 2026-10-10 the bio and interview forms are full sentences with varied structure (subject first, a fronted phrase, an appositive), one trait per sentence, each with its hand-written negated twin ('neg'); in bio sentences {S} is the sentence-initial subject (He or the first name) and {s} the mid-sentence one.

negation.cv: a CV states what a person has, so a negated CV item reads oddly; the nearest form is the item under a label carrying the negation ('Other: not vegan', 'Languages: Welsh (none)' is worse). Code would emit 'not <item>' with the article-free item; to be written per trait (e.g. 'not a twin', 'no motorbike' is a different negation word) and hand-read before use.
negation.form: the field keeps its label and the value is negated: 'Dietary requirements: not vegan', 'Handedness: right' is a contrary rather than a negation and is excluded; per trait a fixed negated value ('Twin: no', 'Vehicle: no motorbike', 'Languages spoken: not Welsh'). Code would map each affirmative value to its 'not <value>' twin; group lines with several values split into one negated line per trait.
negation.bio: each predicate gets a hand-written negated twin with do-support ('is vegan' -> 'is not vegan', 'has a narrowboat' -> 'does not have a narrowboat', 'shoots target archery' -> 'does not shoot target archery'); joined sentences become 'He is not vegan and does not have a narrowboat.' (or 'neither ... nor', a second negation form to avoid). Code would store 'neg' beside each bio phrasing.
negation.interview: the same for first-person clauses ('I'm vegan' -> 'I'm not vegan', 'I've got a narrowboat' -> 'I haven't got a narrowboat'); the frame's open question stays, so the answer reads as a denial of an unasked detail, which is less natural than in the other forms.

bio_conflicts: Withheld for the readout-paraphrase rule (wordings.json 'para'): 'speaks fluent Welsh/Japanese' (the paraphrase question is 'Does X speak Welsh?'), 'owns a narrowboat' / 'owns a motorbike' / 'has his own narrowboat' / 'own motorbike' ('Does X own a narrowboat/motorbike?'), 'plays the cello/bagpipes', 'keeps bees/chickens', 'runs marathons', 'sings in a choir', 'holds a pilot's licence', 'does archery'. The replacements are 'is fluent in Welsh', 'keeps a narrowboat on the canal', 'keeps a motorbike in his garage', 'is a bagpipe player', 'looks after two beehives in his garden', 'has completed several marathons', 'is a member of a community choir', 'shoots target archery'. 2026-10-10 full sentences: 'He sings in a choir' -> 'He sings tenor with a community choir'; 'keeps chickens' -> 'raises chickens' / 'looks after a flock of backyard chickens'; 'He does archery' (and its twin 'does not do archery') -> 'shoots target archery' / 'does not shoot archery'; 'runs marathons' -> 'has completed several marathons' / 'lines up for another marathon'; 'holds a pilot's licence' -> 'gained his private pilot's licence'; teetotal stated outright ('is teetotal and sticks to soft drinks') rather than hinted; egg collecting dropped from the chicken sentences (it bears on veganism); 'drives home' dropped from teetotal (a vehicle); 'Cardiff' dropped from Welsh.
